children: Two-year securities carry a 9.25 per cent annual coupon, with the microfinance lender seeking to diversify its liability mix and reduce borrowing costs
Muthoot Microfin has raised Rs 250 crore through the allotment of listed, rated, secured and redeemable non-convertible debentures (NCDs) on a private placement basis.
The company has allotted 2,50,000 NCDs with a face value of Rs 10,000 each. The securities have a tenure of 24 months and carry a coupon rate of 9.25 per cent a year, payable monthly.
Muthoot Microfin said the fund raise is aimed at strengthening its funding profile, diversifying its liability mix and reducing its overall borrowing costs.
The NCDs are secured by a first-ranking, exclusive charge over the company’s receivables.
Sadaf Sayeed, Chief Executive Officer, Muthoot Microfin, said the Rs 250-crore fund raise would strengthen the company’s funding profile and maintain access to diversified sources of capital.

Sayeed said the company’s cost of funds declined by 75 basis points in financial year 2025-26. He added that the company’s recent credit rating upgrade to CRISIL AA-/Stable would support its ability to raise funds at competitive rates.
The company said the fund raise would also support its focus on margins and business growth over the medium term.
As of 30 June 2026, Muthoot Microfin had 3.25 million active customers across 1,671 branches in 21 states and 392 districts. Its gross loan portfolio stood at Rs 14,457.2 crore.
Muthoot Microfin is part of the Muthoot Pappachan Group and provides microfinance loans, including income-generating loans to women running small businesses.
